summary: Proxy healthcheck auth-header echo consumes per-key quota causing early 429s in private webhook-heavy tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightMap (private deployment in eu-west) reports sudden waves of 429 throttles against their webhook ingestion route after enabling a new upstream healthcheck sidecar in their cluster. The healthcheck agent issues an authenticated GET to /hc every 5s and the proxy is configured to rewrite/forward the customer's X-API-Key header for internal routing.

Impact:
- ~15% of webhook worker requests are receiving 429s intermittently during business hours.
- Customer pipelines backpressure and webhook retries causing visible data lag.

Environment:
- Private control plane (customer-managed VPC) connected via private peering to prod-eu-west region.
- Ingress proxy version: v1.14.2 (customer-supplied sidecar config).
- Rate limiting: per-API-key token buckets (refill interval 60s).

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Deploy healthcheck sidecar that calls GET https://ingress.internal/customer/hc with Authorization: Bearer <api-key> every 5s.
2) Trigger webhook burst (100 concurrent small POSTs) to /webhook/ingest.
3) Observe 429s begin within ~2 minutes and persist until healthcheck is disabled.

Observed behaviour:
- /hc probes appear in token-bucket accounting as normal user requests and consume refill credits.
- Proxy rewrite echoes X-Forwarded-For and X-API-Key headers to origin, causing healthchecks to be attributed to the customer's API key.
- Console shows token bucket depletion for the API key and the tenant; quota panel resets but requests still rejected.

Expected behaviour:
- Healthcheck probes should be either exempt from per-key quota accounting or attributed to an internal service account that doesn't consume tenant credits.

Attachments:
- Customer provided snippets of proxy config, sample logs, and console rate charts (attached in ticket).
steps_to_reproduce: Enable healthcheck sidecar that calls customer ingress with auth header every 5s
Send concurrent webhook POSTs to /webhook/ingest to emulate production burst
Watch token bucket and console quota meters for the customer API key
comments: 2026-03-10 09:22 - Support (Maya): Acknowledged. Collected initial logs and asked customer to temporarily disable the healthcheck to confirm correlation.

2026-03-10 09:35 - Customer (BrightMap): Disabled the sidecar healthcheck. 429s stopped within 90s and webhook throughput returned to normal. Re-enabled on request; 429s resumed. Customer willing to keep disabled while we investigate.

2026-03-11 15:10 - SRE (Omar): Captured ingress-proxy access logs and server-side token-bucket traces. Found repeated entries from path /hc with api_key header. Token accounting shows small (5 token) consumption per probe, which multiplied at 12 probes/min equals a non-trivial drain on refill during low burst windows.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Support (Maya): Suggested temporary workaround: configure sidecar healthcheck to use an internal service account (no tenant credits) or change the probe path to a health endpoint that the ingress marks as internal (ingress.ignore_paths). Customer confirmed they will test service-account approach.

2026-03-13 08:42 - SRE (Omar): Reproduced locally in private-vpc simulator by adding an authenticated GET probe; reproduced token bucket depletion pattern and race with refill window. Filed INT-5421 to track a permanent server-side exemption option for healthcheck paths on private deployments.

2026-03-13 12:00 - Support (Maya): Notified customer of workaround options and ETA for a follow-up patch. Customer accepted service-account workaround and requested a console flag to mark probe paths in the interim.
investigation_notes: Ingress proxy rewrite behavior: proxy currently copies incoming Authorization/X-API-Key headers to upstream; this makes healthchecks indistinguishable from normal client requests in rate accounting.
Token-bucket logs: api_key=ak_live_**** shows repeated small deductions matching probe cadence (5 tokens/probe) leading to early exhaustion during concurrent webhook bursts.
Refill logic: 60s refill window means short bursts are vulnerable if constant periodic probes run at high frequency (multi-probe per sec across many hosts).
NAT/pool effect: customer uses pooled egress addresses which multiplex many container probes into same API key accounting domains, worsening apparent per-key drain across worker fleet.
Private deployment nuance: control plane cannot currently enforce global healthcheck exemptions without customer config because the sidecar lives inside customer's network boundary.
resolution: Mitigation: Customer implemented a dedicated service account for healthchecks (credential without tenant quota) and adjusted probe cadence to 30s; immediate 429 waves stopped. Longer-term fix: INT-5421 opened to add a console toggle and server-side rule to treat configured health endpoints as exempt from per-key quota in Private deployments. SRE notes: small ingress-proxy patch (PR linked) will add header rewrite rules to avoid forwarding tenant API keys for probe paths. Patch scheduled for next private-control-plane release (v1.15.0).
follow_up_actions: INT-5421: Implement console 'healthcheck-exempt-paths' config for private deployments (owner: SRE)
PR 412: ingress-proxy change to omit X-API-Key for known probe paths (owner: infra-engineering)
Customer action: keep healthcheck disabled or use service account until v1.15.0 is available; test with adjusted cadence and confirm no regressions
outcome: Workaround applied by customer (service account + slower cadence). Issue mitigated; permanent feature tracked in INT-5421. Support will follow up when v1.15.0 is scheduled into customer private-control-plane rollout.
